teaser.text: Grainger is the distributor businesses call when a workplace needs the right glove, filter, fitting or tool to keep operating. Its business is simple to state but interesting to unpack: it buys a vast range of supplies, moves them through a service and delivery network, and tries to keep enough of each sale after the costs of doing so.

stock.meta_description: Grainger stock forecast: scenario prices, cash generation, operating drivers and the valuation investors are paying today.
stock.opening: Grainger's weighted forecast reaches $1,387.54 in October 2029. It hinges on continued growth, durable margins and productive buybacks.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Grainger's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Grainger's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast puts GWW at $1,291.58 in October 2027 and $1,334.56 in October 2028. It reaches $1,387.54 in October 2029. Those outcomes imply total returns of negative 2% and positive 2% through the first two windows. The three-year return is positive 7%, including dividends.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Grainger, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: Base earnings rise to $2,184 million and then $2,310 million. They reach $2,438 million in the third forecast year. The path reflects mid-single-digit sales growth and modest margin improvement after the strong 2026 outlook. Bear earnings fall to $2,000 million before weakening further, because demand, freight, mix, and service costs pressure margins. Bull earnings reach $2,311 million initially and $2,731 million by the final date, because share gains, online retention, and distribution productivity continue. High-Touch volume grew 1.4% while the U.S. MRO market contracted, and Endless Assortment operating earnings rose with margin improvement.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Grainger really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is operating cash after capital spending. Grainger’s capital projects include warehouses, automation and technology, so the cash available after investment is more important than operating cash alone. Stock-based pay is also an economic cost, even though it does not leave the bank account in the period it is awarded.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Grainger today?

paragraphs.text: A price-to-earnings ratio, or P/E, shows how much investors pay for each dollar of earnings. Grainger’s forward P/E is below its trailing P/E, which means the market expects earnings to rise. Revenue, book value, free cash flow and dividends tell different stories: sales come before costs, book value misses much of the distribution system’s know-how, free cash flow measures cash left after operations and investment, and dividends measure only cash paid directly to shareholders.

dividend.title: Grainger dividend
dividend.meta_description: Grainger’s dividend forecast rises, while cash coverage has sometimes been strained by payouts above free cash flow.
dividend.opening: Grainger’s forecast dividend per share rises to $9.75, then $10.75, and reaches $11.75. Grainger’s cash has not always covered the dividend: payouts sometimes exceeded free cash flow.
dividend.closing: The full memo also examines Grainger’s business, rivals, management, and risks.

blocks.heading: What does Grainger pay its shareholders over time?

paragraphs.text: Base dividends per share rise to $9.75 and then $10.75. They reach $11.75 as growth decelerates from recent increases. The bear case holds at $9.25 after a pause, while the bull case reaches $13.25 through faster increases. The base reflects uninterrupted historical increases and strong cash-flow guidance, while the bear recognizes working-capital and capital-spending pressure.

blocks.heading: Is Grainger’s dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Grainger’s payouts sometimes exceeded the free cash flow generated in the same year. That is possible because the company can draw down cash already on its balance sheet, issue debt, or accept a smaller cash reserve. Dividends go to all shareholders; buybacks return cash to shareholders who sell their shares and reduce the number of shares left outstanding.

earnings.title: Grainger earnings: guidance and next results
earnings.meta_description: Grainger's next results are expected November 4, 2026; guidance covers sales, EPS, margin and cash, with demand and margins to watch.
earnings.opening: Grainger's next results are expected on November 4, 2026. Watch whether Grainger can preserve margins after the tariff refund fades.
earnings.closing: The full Grainger memo also covers its business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: For 2026, management guides to $19.4–$19.7 billion in sales. It guides to $45.50–$47.25 in diluted EPS. The target operating margin is 15.8%–16.2%. Operating cash flow is targeted at $2.25–$2.4 billion.

blocks.heading: Has Grainger kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: The takeaway is straightforward: Grainger’s system offers formal alignment, and recent payouts show some discipline, but shareholders still must judge the measures, the dilution and the board’s willingness to hold management accountable.

blocks.heading: How has Grainger's revenue and profit changed over the last eight quarters?

paragraphs.text: The June 2026 quarter showed stronger demand. Reported sales growth was 10.3%, while daily, organic constant-currency growth was 13.7%; the difference reflects selling days, currency and exited businesses. Volume and price pass-through helped High-Touch, while Zoro and MonotaRO drove Endless Assortment. Prebuying at MonotaRO may not repeat, so the next question is whether growth becomes profit.

blocks.heading: What should investors watch in Grainger's next results?

paragraphs.text: November 4, 2026, Q3 results test demand and margins as the tariff refund fades, alongside guidance through the CFO transition. In Q4 2026, Nampa distribution center operations are expected to begin. Across results, the decisive signals are High-Touch volume outgrowth, online retention and margins, and operating cash after working capital and capital spending.
